source.title: Gradient Descent Provably Escapes Saddle Points in the Training of Shallow ReLU Networks
source.authors: Patrick Cheridito; Arnulf Jentzen; Florian Rossmannek

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves results for gradient descent on specially structured shallow ReLU and leaky ReLU networks, addressing avoidance of saddle points and convergence to global minima rather than benchmark classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper's results are theoretical. They concern scalar-input, scalar-output networks trained against a one-dimensional affine target under stated assumptions; no CIFAR benchmarks, empirical training runs, or reported training-error measurements appear. The convergence theorem concerns almost all step sizes and a restricted set of convergent initializations whose limiting loss is below a threshold. Other benchmark and recipe findings in the versions are prior-work citations, not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study proves saddle avoidance and conditional convergence for shallow scalar-input networks on affine targets. These results test none of V1–V6: they do not compare student and teacher widths, initialization schemes, depths, normalization, or learning rates relative to stability thresholds. The V2 original is cited as prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors extend center-stable manifold theory to weaker regularity settings and prove avoidance of specified saddle points. Global-minimum convergence is conditional on trajectory convergence: ReLU additionally requires a limiting-loss threshold, while leaky ReLU requires a sufficiently small activation parameter and a nondegenerate limit.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proves dynamical-systems results for gradient descent on shallow networks with scalar input and affine targets, rather than testing random-initialization training error on image-classification benchmarks. It also analyzes a generalized gradient at nondifferentiable points.
record.method_sensitivity: Theorems require almost all step sizes; ReLU global-minimum convergence requires a specified limiting-loss bound and, in Proposition 4.8(i), no degenerate neurons at the limit. The leaky ReLU results require ζ below ζ₀ depending on N, and convergence in Corollary 5.5 assumes a convergent limit without degenerate neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: For even-width shallow ReLU networks, almost every qualifying convergent initialization reaches zero integral squared loss for almost every positive step size, provided limiting loss is below the stated width-dependent threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent conditionally reaches global minima for shallow scalar-input ReLU networks fitting nonconstant affine targets.

fits_no_version.finding: For almost every positive step size, initializations converging to the specified nondegenerate ReLU saddle-point set have Lebesgue measure zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent almost surely avoids the specified saddle points in shallow ReLU affine-target regression.

fits_no_version.finding: For a sufficiently small width-dependent leaky ReLU parameter and almost every positive step size, initializations converging to nondegenerate saddle points have Lebesgue measure zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent almost surely avoids nondegenerate saddle points in the studied leaky ReLU affine-target regression problem.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the leaky ReLU parameter restriction, almost every initialization whose trajectory converges to a nondegenerate limit reaches zero loss for almost every positive step size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergent shallow leaky ReLU trajectories with nondegenerate limits conditionally reach global minima on affine targets.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
record.problems: The results are theoretical and narrowly specialized to scalar-input, scalar-output shallow networks with affine targets and squared L2 loss. The ReLU global-minimum result has restrictive convergence and limiting-loss conditions; the leaky ReLU results require a width-dependent parameter threshold. The text provides no empirical benchmark training-error measurements or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable results omitted. Claims about overparameterization, linearization and kernels in the infinite-width regime, initialization geometry, and empirical or other cited findings are literature discussion or cited prior work, not results measured by this study.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, corrupted labels, network size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student width comparisons, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh initialization, and normalization-free residual training.
Comparative initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability training.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical results can test a version, but these concern different outcomes and settings. Almost-every-step-size saddle avoidance does not guarantee trajectory convergence or recovery above a stability threshold. Row states indicate inability to determine the listed versions, not a failure of the stated theorems.

versions.untested_parts: Benchmark classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student networks, spurious-minimum frequency as width grows, and student width exceeding teacher width.
Depth, batch normalization, identity shortcuts, ImageNet/CIFAR-10 training error, and Fixup results.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, comparative initialization speeds, and very deep tanh or convolutional networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss/curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance and Fixup's normalization-free results.

rows.note: A conditional theoretical guarantee, not an empirical benchmark result. The set of qualifying initializations is specified using convergence and a bound on the limiting loss; this is not a general claim about random initialization.
rows.check: The conditional zero integral-loss theorem is correctly reported, but it cannot establish any listed version. It assumes trajectory convergence and a limiting-loss bound rather than demonstrating benchmark classification performance from standard random initialization.

rows.value: The set has Lebesgue measure zero
rows.note: S excludes saddle points solely composed of inactive neurons and semi-inactive neurons satisfying the stated sign condition. This is a saddle-avoidance theorem, not a reported training-error value.
rows.check: Saddle avoidance does not measure V2's frequency of convergence to spurious local minima or its width intervention. Explicitly include that S contains only networks without degenerate neurons, in addition to the stated exclusions.
